717: volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_sync_cnt = 0;
718: 
719: static bk_err_t mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd_sync(u8 log_chnl, mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_ptr)
720: {
721: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
722: 	u16 			chnl_type;
723: 
724: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
725: 
726: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
727: 
728: #if !CONFIG_SOC_SMP
729: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
730: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
731: #endif
732: 
733: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
734: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
735: 
736: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
737: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
738: 
739: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
740: 
741: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = log_chnl;
742: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq = 0;
743: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl  = CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX;
744: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.state = 0;
745: 
746: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL;
747: 
748: 	s_mailbox_sync_cnt++;
749: 
750: 	/*
751: 	 * can't wait 'phy_chnl_cb.tx_state' to be CHNL_STATE_IDLE here,
752: 	 * 'phy_chnl_cb.tx_state' is set to CHNL_STATE_IDLE in interrupt callback.
753: 	 * but the interrupt may be disabled when this API is called.
754: 	 *    wait physical channel HW to be IDLE by <POLLing> !!
755: 	 */
756: 	while(1)
757: 	{
758: 		ret_code = bk_mailbox_send_safe((mailbox_data_t *)cmd_ptr, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
759: 
760: 		if(ret_code != BK_ERR_MAILBOX_TIMEOUT)
761: 		{
762: 			break;
763: 		}
764: 	}
765: 
766: 	return ret_code;
767: }

770: /* =====================      logical channel APIs      ==================*/
771: /*
772:   * init logical chnanel module.
773:   * return:
774:   *     succeed: BK_OK;
775:   *     failed  : fail code.
776:   *
777:   */
778: bk_err_t mb_chnl_init(void)
779: {
780: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
781: 	int				i, j;
782: 
783: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
784: 
785: 	/*
786: 	 * mb_chnl_init() is reached from mb_chnl_open(), which is called by
787: 	 * many subsystems (shell log forwarding, ipc_init, mb_uart, ...).
788: 	 * Each one of those callers runs on its own FreeRTOS task and they
789: 	 * can race here:
790: 	 *
791: 	 *   Task A: enters mb_chnl_open(MB_CHNL_LOG), sees mb_chnnl_init_ok==0,
792: 	 *           enters mb_chnl_init(), runs all the memset's, sets
793: 	 *           mb_chnnl_init_ok=1, returns. Caller then sets
794: 	 *           log_chnl_cb2[15].in_used=1 and installs rx_isr.
795: 	 *   Task B (preempted in the middle of mb_chnl_open before the
796: 	 *           init_ok check finishes): comes back, sees init_ok still
797: 	 *           == 0 (because it sampled before A set it), enters
798: 	 *           mb_chnl_init() AGAIN, and the memset wipes the
799: 	 *           log_chnl_cb_x[] array that A just populated.
800: 	 *
801: 	 * Fix: serialize the body with the existing critical section so the
802: 	 * "if (init_ok) return; ... init_ok = 1;" sequence is atomic w.r.t.
803: 	 * other tasks. The double-check pattern still keeps the fast path
804: 	 * lock-free once init has completed.
805: 	 */
806: 	if(mb_chnnl_init_ok)

983: bk_err_t mb_chnl_write(u8 log_chnl, mb_chnl_cmd_t * cmd_buf)
984: {
985: 	u16		write_len;
986: 
987: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
988: 	u8		log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);

990: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
991: 
992: #if !CONFIG_SOC_SMP
993: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
994: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
995: #endif

997: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
998: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;

1001: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
1002: 
1003: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
1004: 
1005: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
1006: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
1007: 
1008: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].in_used == 0)
1009: 		return BK_ERR_STATE;
1010: 
1011: 	u32 int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
1012: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t *phy = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
1013: 	mb_chnl_cmd_t *logical_cmd = cmd_buf;
1014: 
1015: 	if (phy->recovering &&
1016: 		!(log_chnl == MB_CHNL_UART0 &&
1017: 		  logical_cmd->hdr.cmd == MB_UART_STATE_COMMAND))
1018: 	{
1019: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
1020: 		return BK_ERR_BUSY;
1021: 	}
1022: 
1023: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
1024: 	{
1025: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
1026: 
1027: 		return BK_ERR_BUSY;
1028: 	}
1029: 
1030: 	write_len = sizeof(mailbox_data_t) > sizeof(mb_chnl_cmd_t) ? sizeof(mb_chnl_cmd_t) : sizeof(mailbox_data_t);
1031: 
1032: 	memset(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, 0,
1033: 	       sizeof(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff));
1034: 	memcpy(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, cmd_buf, write_len);
1035: 
1036: 	/* set to BUSY means there is data in tx-buff. mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr will get it to send. */
1037: 	log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;   /* MUST set to BUSY after data was copied. */
1038: 	__DMB();
1039: 
1040: 	bk_err_t start_ret = mb_phy_chnl_start_tx(log_chnl);
1041: 
1042: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
1043: 
1044: 	return start_ret;
1045: }

1067: #if !CONFIG_SOC_SMP

1069: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
1070: #endif
1071: 
1072: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.

1074: 
1075: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)

1080: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])

1083: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].in_used == 0)
1084: 		return BK_ERR_STATE;

1089:

1091: 				return BK_ERR_NULL_PARAM;

1094: 
1095: 			break;
1096: 
1097: 		case MB_CHNL_SET_RX_ISR:
1098: 			log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr = (chnl_rx_isr_t)param;
1099: 			break;
1100: 
1101: 		case MB_CHNL_SET_TX_ISR:
1102: 			log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr = (chnl_tx_isr_t)param;
1103: 			break;
1104:

1117: 			return ret_code;
1118: 			break;
1119: 
1120: 		default:
1121: 			return BK_ERR_NOT_SUPPORT;

1128: void mb_chnl_poll(void)
1129: {
1130: 	u8 phy_idx;
1131: 
1132: 	bk_mailbox_poll();
1133: 	mb_chnl_ack_retry();
1134: 
1135: 	for (phy_idx = 0; phy_idx < PHY_CHNL_NUM; phy_idx++)
1136: 	{
1137: 		mb_phy_chnl_cb_t *phy = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_idx];
1138: 		mb_log_chnl_cb_t *logs;
1139: 		mb_chnl_ack_t failure;
1140: 		u8 log_idx;
1141: 
1142: 		u32 claim_flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
1143: 		if ((phy->tx_state != CHNL_STATE_BUSY) || !phy->busy_since_ms ||
1144: 			((u32)(rtos_get_time() - phy->busy_since_ms) < MB_PHY_CHNL_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS))
1145: 		{
1146: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(claim_flags);
1147: 			continue;
1148: 		}
1149: 		phy->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
1150: 		phy->busy_since_ms = 0;
1151: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(claim_flags);
1152: 
1153: 		logs = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_idx];
1154: 		log_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(phy->tx_log_chnl);
1155: 		if (log_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx])
1156: 			continue;
1157: 
1158: 		phy->tx_fault_cnt++;
1159: 		phy->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x20000000;
1160: 		bk_mailbox_tx_timeout((mailbox_endpoint_t)phy_idx);
1161: 		phy->recovering = 1;
1162: 		memset(&failure, 0, sizeof(failure));
1163: 		failure.hdr.cmd = phy->tx_hdr_cmd;
1164: 		failure.hdr.state = CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;
1165: 		if (logs[log_idx].tx_cmpl_isr)
1166: 			logs[log_idx].tx_cmpl_isr(logs[log_idx].isr_param, &failure);
1167: 		mb_chnl_fail_pending(logs, phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx]);
1168: 		mb_chnl_notify(logs, phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx],
1169: 				   MB_CHNL_EVENT_TX_TIMEOUT);
1170: 		if (mb_phy_chnl_send_reset(phy_idx, phy->tx_log_chnl) == BK_OK)
1171: 			mb_chnl_notify(logs, phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx],
1172: 					   MB_CHNL_EVENT_ABORT_SENT);
1173: 		else
1174: 			mb_chnl_notify(logs, phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx],
1175: 					   MB_CHNL_EVENT_ABORT_FAILED);
1176: 	}
1177: }

57: static void mbox0_reap_slots(u8 dst)
58: {
59: 	mbox0_tx_slots_t *slots;
60: 	uint32_t fifo_count;
61: 	u32 reaped = 0;
62: 	u32 now;
63: 	u8 i;
64: 
65: 	if (mbox0_drv_get_send_count(dst, &fifo_count) != MBOX0_HAL_OK)
66: 		return;
67: 
68: 	slots = &mailbox_slots[dst];
69: 	if (fifo_count != 0)
70: 	{
71: 		slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = 0;
72: 		return;
73: 	}
74: 
75: 	now = rtos_get_time();
76: 	if (!slots->fifo_empty_since_ms)
77: 	{
78: 		slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = now ? now : 1;
79: 		return;
80: 	}
81: 	if ((u32)(now - slots->fifo_empty_since_ms) <
82: 		MBOX0_SLOT_QUARANTINE_MS)
83: 		return;
84: 
85: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_CMD_SLOT_NUM; i++)
86: 	{
87: 		reaped += slots->cmd_used[i] != 0;
88: 		slots->cmd_used[i] = 0;
89: 	}
90: 	/* ACK slots are released only by a later command ACK fence.  FIFO empty
91: 	 * alone does not prove that the peer finished copying the pointed data.
92: 	 */
93: 	reaped += slots->reset_used != 0;
94: 	reaped += slots->sync_used != 0;
95: 	slots->reset_used = 0;
96: 	slots->sync_used = 0;
97: 	slots->cmd_active = 0;
98: 	slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = 0;
99: 	adapter_diag.tx_reaped += reaped;
100: }

151: 				*kind = 1;
152: 				*index = i;
153: 				return &slots->ack[i];
154: 			}
155: 		}
156: 		return NULL;
157: 	}

160: 	{
161: 		if (slots->sync_used)
162: 			return NULL;
163: 		slots->sync_used = 1;
164: 		slots->sync_order = ++slots->publish_order;
165: 		*kind = 3;

250: static void mbox0_rx_isr(mbox0_message_t *msg)
251: {
252: 	u32 address;
253: 	u32 source;
254: 	mbox0_rx_desc_t *desc;
255: 	u8 i;
256:

258: 		return;

262: 	{
263: 		adapter_diag.bad_sid++;
264: 		return;
265: 	}
266: 	if (msg->data[1] != sizeof(mailbox_data_t))
267: 	{
268: 		adapter_diag.bad_length++;
269: 		return;
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	address = msg->data[0];

274: 	{
275: 		adapter_diag.bad_alignment++;
276: 		return;
277: 	}
278: 	if (address > UINT32_MAX - sizeof(mailbox_data_t) ||
279: 		address < MBOX0_AP_RAM_START ||
280: 		address + sizeof(mailbox_data_t) > MBOX0_AP_RAM_END)
281: 	{
282: 		adapter_diag.bad_address++;
283: 		return;
284: 	}
285: 	if (rx_count >= MBOX0_RX_DESC_NUM)
286: 	{
287: 		adapter_diag.descriptor_overflow++;
288: 		return;
289: 	}

291: #if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
292: 	SCB_InvalidateDCache_by_Addr((void *)address, sizeof(mailbox_data_t));
293: #endif
294: 	__DMB();
295: 	desc = NULL;
296: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_RX_DESC_NUM; i++)
297: 	{
298: 		if (!rx_desc[i].used)
299: 		{
300: 			desc = &rx_desc[i];
301: 			break;
302: 		}
303: 	}
304: 	if (!desc)
305: 	{
306: 		adapter_diag.descriptor_overflow++;
307: 		return;
308: 	}
309: 	memcpy(&desc->data, (void *)address, sizeof(desc->data));
310: 	desc->source = source;
311: 	desc->order = ++rx_order;
312: 	desc->used = 1;
313: 	rx_count++;

151: 
152: 	while (ssid) {
153: 		if (!wpas_network_disabled(wpa_s, ssid))
154: 			count++;

170: static void wpa_supplicant_assoc_try(struct wpa_supplicant *wpa_s,
171: 				     struct wpa_ssid *ssid)
172: {
173: 	int min_temp_disabled = 0;
174: 
175: 	while (ssid) {
176: 		if (!wpas_network_disabled(wpa_s, ssid)) {
177: 			int temp_disabled = wpas_temp_disabled(wpa_s, ssid);
178: 
179: 			if (temp_disabled <= 0)
180: 				break;
181: 
182: 			if (!min_temp_disabled ||
183: 			    temp_disabled < min_temp_disabled)
184: 				min_temp_disabled = temp_disabled;
185: 		}
186: 		ssid = ssid->next;
187: 	}
188: 
189: 	/* ap_scan=2 mode - try to associate with each SSID. */
190: 	if (ssid == NULL) {
191: 		wpa_dbg(wpa_s, MSG_DEBUG, "wpa_supplicant_assoc_try: Reached "
192: 			"end of scan list - go back to beginning");
193: 		wpa_s->prev_scan_ssid = WILDCARD_SSID_SCAN;
194: 		wpa_supplicant_req_scan(wpa_s, min_temp_disabled, 0);
195: 		return;
196: 	}
197: 	if (ssid->next) {
198: 		/* Continue from the next SSID on the next attempt. */
199: 		wpa_s->prev_scan_ssid = ssid;
200: 	} else {
201: 		/* Start from the beginning of the SSID list. */
202: 		wpa_s->prev_scan_ssid = WILDCARD_SSID_SCAN;
203: 	}
204: 	wpa_supplicant_associate(wpa_s, NULL, ssid);
205: }

284: static int netdev_upper_txpoll(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
285: {
286:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper = dev->d_private;
287:   FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower = upper->lower;

291:   DEBUGASSERT(dev->d_len > 0);

293:   NETDEV_TXPACKETS(dev);

295: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_PKT
296:   /* When packet sockets are enabled, loopback the tx frame to pkt socket
297:    * who has protocl type of ETH_P_ALL

300:   pkt_loopback(dev);
301: #endif

303:   pkt = netpkt_get(dev, NETPKT_TX);

305:   if (netpkt_getdatalen(lower, pkt) > NETDEV_PKTSIZE(dev))
306:     {

308:       ret = -EMSGSIZE;
309:     }

312:       ret = lower->ops->transmit(lower, pkt);

**Findings**
1. **Critical: carrier notifications invert the network and packet-lock order, allowing a permanent deadlock during disconnect/reset.** The Wi-Fi worker acquires `packet_lock` and processes command events while retaining it at [bk7258_wifi.c:1198](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1198) and [bk7258_wifi.c:1231](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1231). A disconnect event calls `wifi_set_carrier(false)` at [bk7258_wifi.c:621](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:621), which enters `netdev_lower_carrier_off()` from [bk7258_wifi.c:325](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:325) and waits for the network lock. Conversely, NuttX holds the network lock while calling the lower-half `transmit()` at [netdev_upperhalf.c:388](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/net/netdev_upperhalf.c:388) and [netdev_upperhalf.c:312](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/net/netdev_upperhalf.c:312), and `wifi_transmit()` then waits for `packet_lock` at [bk7258_wifi.c:1269](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1269). Concurrent TX and disconnect therefore produce `netdev lock -> packet_lock` against `packet_lock -> netdev lock`.

2. **Critical: mailbox link-state coalescing can hide a peer reset from the Wi-Fi driver, after which stale shared-memory pointers can be processed.** `set_link_state()` overwrites a single `g_diag_state` for every transition and only posts a semaphore at [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:246](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:246). The diagnostic worker snapshots only the latest state at [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:790](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:790), so a rapid `ABORTING -> PROBING -> READY` sequence can deliver only `READY`. `wifi_link_changed()` immediately ignores `READY` at [bk7258_wifi.c:1118](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1118), leaving `g_wifi.reset_generation` unchanged and old queued nodes unpurged.
